metadata.title: Human-verified bat acoustics: bat calls and noise
metadata.description:
This dataset contains manually validated bat echolocation recordings and noise samples derived from passive acoustic monitoring using AudioMoth devices. The dataset consists of short audio segments in which bat calls were first detected using automated algorithms and subsequently verified by an expert.

Audio segment characteristics

The dataset includes audio segments of varying duration:

  • 5-second segments
    Derived from systematic acoustic sampling without amplitude threshold filtering. Due to the subsampling of recordings (e.g. multiple short segments within the same minute), identical filenames may occur. These are renamed as: filename.wav, filename(2).wav, filename(3).wav, ...
  • Variable-length segments
    Derived from alternative sampling protocols in which amplitude-based filters were applied prior to selection

Acoustic pre-processing

Initial screening of recordings was performed using the BTO Acoustic Pipeline (British Trust for Ornithology, UK):
https://www.bto.org/data/tools-products/acoustic-pipeline

This automated step was used to detect and pre-classify segments with potential bat calls. In Rstudio, these identified segments were exported separetely.

Manual validation and species assignment

Manual validation was performed to establish reliable species presence per sampling location.

For each audio segment:

  • Presence of bat calls was confirmed or rejected
  • When possible, calls were assigned to species level
  • When calls could not be reliably distinguished, they were assigned to a confusion group (acoustic complex)

If only one species within a confusion complex was confidently identified at a given location, all recordings belonging to that complex at that location were attributed to that species. File-level labels may hence reflect context-based assignment, not strictly call-level certainty

Dataset contents

The dataset contains both validated bat call recordings and noise recordings (segments without bat calls that were retained with the pre-classifier). Segments with multiple identified species will occur once for each species attributed.

File naming convention

Filenames are structured to encode key metadata:

<SPECIES_CODE>_<LAT>_<LON>_<DATE>_<TIME>[_ADDITIONAL_INFO].wav
  • SPECIES_CODE:
    Abbreviated species name or acoustic group code
  • LAT, LON:
    Recording coordinates (decimal degrees)
  • DATE:
    Format: YYYYMMDD
  • TIME:
    Format: HHMM (local time)
  • ADDITIONAL_INFO:
    May include additional species detected in the same segment or other annotations

Important considerations for reuse

  • The dataset represents validated detections, not continuous recordings
  • Species labels may reflect site-level inference within acoustic complexes
  • Noise files are included and can be used for classifier training or benchmarking
  • Absence of a species in the dataset does not necessarily imply true absence at a site
  • Current version contains data on 27 agroforestry-like sites across Flanders, a region with poor species richness. Later updates will include sites in Portugal, Spain, Czechia, France and the UK.
